description: Revising the qualifications of Guarantors to be presented for obtaining loans under the Interest-Free Student Loan Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-12-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - An interest-free student loan scheme has been initiated from the year 2017 for students who have passed the Advanced Level to pursue government-recognized degree courses in non-government higher education institutions. At present, 23,162 students under nine intakes have been benefitted under the said interest-free student loan scheme, and of them, 5,772 students have completed their degrees by now. From the first intake to the sixth intake of the said loan scheme, the opportunity has been given to present a close relative along with the mother/father or guardian of the students as guarantors. Nevertheless, those conditions have been amended from the year 2022 so that students applying for loans must present their mother/father or guardian as the first guarantor and a person with an income determined by the bank as the second guarantor. In this backdrop, it has been reported that students who must necessarily obtain loans under the said loan scheme are facing inconveniences. At the preliminary meeting held regarding the budget proposals for the year 2026, the Hon. President has instructed to take steps to continue the said loan scheme and to provide the opportunity to present guarantors in a manner that does not cause any hindrance to students. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to provide the opportunity for students to obtain loans by presenting the mother/father or guardian as the first guarantor and a close relative as the second guarantor from the 9th intake of the said loan scheme, was approved by the Cabinet.
